definitions.gloss: precariousness; the quality of being on the edge of failure
definitions.explanation: The nominalized form of {危|あや}うい. It names a fragile, unstable quality that could tip into disaster at any moment — often used admiringly of art, performance, or beauty as well as critically of situations.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{危|あや}うさ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: I noticed how precarious that plan was.
Her singing has both a fragility and a beauty to it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{好調|こうちょう}→好調：12209_kouchou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{経済|けいざい}→経済：01394_keizai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦{一部|いちぶ}→一部：06783_ichibu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{専門家|せんもんか}→専門家：03088_senmonka⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{危|あや}うさ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じている→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: Even in this economy, which looks strong, some experts sense a fragility.

notes:
Formed from the i-adjective ⟦{危|あや}うい→危うい：11825_ayaui⟧ plus the nominalizing suffix 〜さ. Written language more than conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {危|あや}うさ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧: to sense a precariousness
- {危|あや}うさ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧はらむ: to contain an element of danger
- {危|あや}うさ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{漂|ただよ}う→漂う：04356_tadayou⟧: an air of fragility hangs over something
- ⟦ぎりぎり→ぎりぎり：05166_girigiri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{危|あや}うさ: a razor's-edge precariousness

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {危|あぶ}なさ: dangerousness — plainer and more physical; {危|あや}うさ is more literary and often admiring
- ⟦{危険|きけん}{性|せい}→危険性：17827_kikensei⟧: riskiness — neutral and analytical, used in reports and assessments
